one_month_reasoning: Window Oct 6 - Nov 5, 2026. Unlike the 2026-09-29 window, Amazon's Q3 print falls inside it: expected Thu Oct 29 after the close (Trefis; Amazon has not yet posted a webcast notice, so the date is unconfirmed). Guidance is sales $197-202B (+9-12%, held down because Prime Day moved into June) and operating income $22.5-26.5B vs $17.4B a year ago. Consensus Q3 is EPS $1.95 and revenue $202.03B, at the top of the guide, so the headline beat will be small and the stock will trade on AWS growth versus Azure and Google Cloud, the Q4 guide and the first 2027 capex framing. Other events in the window: Prime Big Deal Days Oct 6-7, the Oct 7 AWS Capacity Block price rise (~15%), Microsoft and Alphabet results expected around Oct 27 (cloud growth and capex read-through; the standing capex file notes guides only went up in 2026), the Oct 28 FOMC after the Sep 16 hike, and a possible public Anthropic S-1. Industry evidence leans mildly positive: GPU pricing is firm (AWS hike, H100 index +16% y/y) and Micron's FQ1 guide of $61.5B confirms demand. But another capex raise and the $8B off-balance-sheet chip SPV headline are two-sided. I center the 1-month distribution at +0.4% (~$257), with sigma ~10.5% plus a fat-tail component for the earnings gap. That is wider than the plain monthly vol (34%/3.5 = 9.7%) because the print is in the window.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of forward P/E ($285: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 $12.38 = 25% FY27 consensus $10.51 + 75% FY28 $13.00 [consensus $13.81 haircut ~6% for depreciation], x 23x vs a 10-peer CY2027 median of 23.8x) and a sum of the parts ($271: AWS $1.81T + retail/ads $1.00T + Anthropic ~$0.16T after tax - Leo $0.05T - net debt $30.9B - Globalstar $10.9B, over 10.90B diluted shares = $264.7, rolled forward 2.5%).

inputs_detail.input: FY2026 normalized consensus EPS (context for growth)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $13.81 haircut ~6%: TTM capex $173.0B already above TTM OCF $161.4B (FCF -$7.6B), Amazon's 2027 capex consensus is $256.5-319.1B vs ~$220B in 2026 (standing capex file, secondary), and Micron's 87% gross margin and +13% q/q FQ1 guide say memory costs inside that capex keep rising, so FY28 depreciation growth is likely under-modelled. 13.00/10.51 = +23.7%.

Peer median CY2027 P/E 23.8x (range 6.5-77.8x); AMZN trades at 24.4x CY2027 today ($256.29 / $10.51). I use 23x, slightly below the median and inside the range: AMZN's EPS growth (+31% consensus FY28) is above the peer median (+19.7%), but its FCF is negative while MSFT/GOOGL/META generate FCF, the Fed is hiking (target 3.75-4.00% from Sep 17), and the market has cut Oracle, the other debt-funded AI-capex builder, to 17.6x. No premium claimed.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: AWS 2027E revenue $230B x 38% margin x (1-17% tax) = $72.5B NOPAT x 25 = $1,813.6B; retail+ads 2027E OI $55B x 0.83 x 22 = $1,004.3B; Anthropic ~$160B after tax; Leo -$50B; net debt -$30.9B; Globalstar -$10.9B; total $2,886.1B / 10.903B diluted shares = $264.7; x 1.025 roll-forward = $271

inputs_detail.derivation: Run-rate $168.8B growing ~30-35% in 2026-27 on $496B commitments; the cloud market grew 43% in Q2 (Synergy) while AWS grew 37%, so AWS keeps losing share (28% vs MSFT 20%, Google 15%) and I do not assume re-acceleration. Pricing is firm: AWS raises Capacity Block GPU prices ~15% on Oct 7 (P6-B300 $14.04 -> $16.146) and the H100 rental index is +16% y/y, which argues against a near-term price war but Capacity Blocks are too small a product to raise the revenue estimate.
Q2 reported 39.3%, trimmed ~1.3pt for depreciation of 2026-27 capex whose memory content is getting dearer (Micron non-GAAP GM 87.0%)
Carried judgment from 2026-09-29 for a normalized rate excluding Anthropic mark-to-market gains; not a reported figure

Cross-check against peers: AWS 2027 EBITDA ~ OI $87.4B + ~$50B D&A (my estimate) = ~$137B, so $1.81T is ~13.2x, below MSFT 14.4x and GOOGL 13.9x CY2027 EV/EBITDA and above ORCL 8.4x. AWS is the share leader but is losing share, so I place it under the two faster-growing hyperscalers.

Q2-26 North America $9.1B + International $1.7B = $10.8B x 4 = $43.2B annualized; ads +26% y/y plus logistics leverage lift it ~27% to $55B in 2027. US online holiday spend is forecast +6.7% (Adobe), so growth is margin-led, not demand-led; Walmart's EPS growth (+10.6%) bounds the retail peer set.
Between ad peer META (21.8x P/E) and US retail peers WMT 33.0x / COST 39.3x, above China e-commerce (BABA 15.0x, PDD 6.5x); EV/EBITDA ~11x sits inside the retail range 2.3-23.8x

bear.story: Oracle-style de-rating: AI demand digests or a lab customer stumbles, AWS slows toward the mid-20s while Azure and Google keep taking share in a 40%+ market, 2027 capex rises again on memory prices (Micron GM 87%) so FCF stays negative and the off-balance-sheet chip SPVs read as financing stress, and the Fed keeps hiking. NTM EPS ~$10.8 x ~17x (where ORCL trades today) = ~$185.

base.story: AWS grows ~30% on the $496B backlog with firm GPU pricing (Capacity Blocks +15% on Oct 7, H100 index +16% y/y), ads compound in the mid-20s, normalized EPS reaches ~$13 in FY28 (a bit under the $13.81 consensus), capex growth slows in 2027-28, and the multiple stays ~23x NTM EPS of ~$12.4, near the peer median.

bull.story: AWS re-accelerates toward 40% as Trainium capacity (Synopsys IP deal, Anthropic capacity ramp) lands and pricing keeps rising, FCF turns positive in 2027, FY28 EPS beats $13.81, and an Anthropic IPO well above the $190B carrying value crystallizes the stake; ~26x on NTM EPS ~$13.4.

comps_summary.peer_range: Basis: 10 peers, all from MarketScreener consensus pages on 2026-10-06, calendarized to CY2027 (Dec-FY names use FY2027; MSFT 0.5 FY27 + 0.5 FY28; ORCL 5/12 FY27 + 7/12 FY28; WMT FY Jan-28; COST 8/12 FY27 + 4/12 FY28; BABA 3/12 FY27 + 9/12 FY28). P/E = price / CY27 EPS, or MarketScreener P/E rescaled by EPS for the CNY-reporting BABA and PDD. EV/EBITDA = (EV/Sales x Sales) / CY27 EBITDA. Fwd P/E 6.5x (PDD) to 77.8x (SHOP), median 23.8x. Fwd EV/EBITDA 2.3x (PDD) to 53.2x (SHOP), median 13.7x. Next-year EPS growth median +19.7%. Coupang was considered and excluded: CY27 EPS of $0.35 after a 2026 loss gives a meaningless 40x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: AMZN today: 24.4x CY27 P/E ($256.29 / $10.51) and 10.4x CY27 EV/EBITDA (EV ~$2.84T / $273.5B EBITDA). Its EV/EBITDA is low because of very high D&A. Our P/E leg uses 23x NTM EPS, 0.8x below the peer median and well inside the range. The SOTP implies ~13x EV/EBITDA for AWS (below MSFT 14.4x and GOOGL 13.9x) and ~11x for retail/ads (inside the 2.3-23.8x retail range).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is applied. AMZN's consensus EPS growth (+31% FY28) is well above the peer median (+19.7%), which on its own would argue for a premium. Two persistent factors offset it through the horizon. First, FCF is negative (TTM capex $173B vs OCF $161B) while the closest cloud/ads peers MSFT, GOOGL and META are FCF-positive. Second, the market is visibly penalizing debt-funded AI capex: ORCL trades at 17.6x and AMZN is now moving chips into an $8B off-balance-sheet SPV. Add an active Fed hiking cycle and a multiple slightly under the median follows. MS's growth-adjusted framing (AMZN ~0.5x 2028 EV/EBIT/growth vs ~0.5x median, MS 2026-10-04 p.4) also says AMZN is roughly in line with peers, not cheap; I give it low weight.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at $185. That is 27.8% below today's $256.29, below the $196 52-week low, and 17.6x FY27 consensus EPS of $10.51, exactly where Oracle (the market's example of stressed, debt-funded AI capex) trades on CY27 today. For AMZN to reach that multiple while consensus still says +26% EPS growth in 2027 would most likely mean a structural break: AWS slowing toward the low 20s while the cloud market grows 40%+ (share loss turning competitive), an AI-lab backlog renegotiation, GPU rental pricing rolling over (the AWS Capacity Block and H100 indices are the early warning), or credit stress visible in the off-balance-sheet chip financing. A 34%-vol year alone does not get there.

reasoning: Delta refresh of the 2026-09-29 industry-lane work. (1) Stock: +3.9% since Sep 29 ($246.67 -> $256.29) against QQQ +2.9%, MSFT +4.0% and GOOGL +2.0%, so the move is mostly market beta plus ~1pt of idiosyncratic strength (coinciding with Prime Big Deal Days). No new Amazon 8-K or 10-Q: EDGAR shows only a Form 4 since Sep 24 (source 33). (2) Industry evidence since Sep 29: AWS's own pricing page confirms Capacity Block GPU prices rise ~15% on Oct 7 (P6-B300 $14.04 -> $16.146; P5 $5.191 -> $5.970). The getdeploying H100 index is $3.47, +16% y/y, and MS's Compute Desk B300 index is up >50% YTD. Micron (Sep 30) printed $54.2B at 87% GM and guided $61.5B. Synopsys signed a >$1B license-plus-royalty silicon IP deal for Trainium/Graviton/Nitro. Reuters/FT report Amazon is weighing an $8B Grace Blackwell SPV leaseback. Synergy's Q2 report (opened directly this time) shows the cloud market +43%, i.e. faster than AWS's +37%. Net: pricing and demand are firmer than my 25% bear case assumed a week ago, but capex intensity and financing optics are worse, so I hold the bear weight at 25% and tie the bear price to Oracle's multiple. (3) Consensus: FY27 EPS $10.51 (from $10.48; 2 up and 0 down revisions in 7 days); FY26 normalized $8.31 (vs $8.15 cited last week; the S&P Global page now shows $8.31). New: FY28 consensus $13.81 (MarketScreener), +31%. I previously assumed +20% ($12.6). I now use $13.00, a ~6% haircut to consensus for depreciation. (4) Peer set built for the first time on one basis (10 names, CY2027, MarketScreener): median P/E 23.8x, median EV/EBITDA 13.7x. I keep 23x. (5) The SOTP arithmetic is corrected: 230 x 0.38 x 0.83 x 25 = $1.81T for AWS, not the $1.77T written last week. Diluted shares are 10.903B (reported), not 10.95B. Fair value moves $271 -> $278 (P/E $277 -> $285, SOTP $266 -> $271). The ladder is a two-lognormal mixture (82%: median $268, sigma 0.29; 18%: median $260, sigma 0.46), giving a median ~$267 (+4% vs spot, shrinking my +8.5% fair-value gap about halfway toward spot for model risk), a mean ~$281 and P(>=spot) 0.554. Scenario mean $274. Research: ~30 queries/fetches. Twelve Data statistics and estimates were paywalled and Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so consensus came from Yahoo, stockanalysis and MarketScreener. SEC refused the generic user agent, so filings were read via WebFetch. No option prices or implied volatility were used.
